sections.h2: Where do I go for property tax questions in Marion County, KY?
sections.html:
Go to 223 North Spalding Avenue in Lebanon. The sheriff, the Property Valuation Administrator and the County Clerk all list that address, each in its own suite, so one trip can cover a bill, an assessment question and a deed.

  • Sheriff's Office, Suite 101: collects the bill. Phone 270-692-3051, open weekdays 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.
  • Property Valuation Administrator, Suite 202: assessed value, name and address changes, homestead and disability exemptions. Phone 270-692-3401, weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • County Clerk, Suite 102: records deeds and holds delinquent bills. Phone 270-692-2651. The clerk's site lists hours of 8:20 to 4:20 on weekdays and Saturday mornings.

The sheriff's own FAQ sends questions about how a taxable value is set or how a bill is figured to the PVA, and questions about delinquent bills or buying a lien to the clerk. Starting at the right door saves a second trip.

sections.h2: What is Marion County, Kentucky like for someone selling a home?
sections.html:
Marion County is a lightly populated central Kentucky county of about 20,000 people with Lebanon as its seat and largest city. The Kentucky legislature formed it in 1834 from part of Washington County and named it for Revolutionary War officer Francis Marion. It covers 347 square miles, 343 of them land, and touches Washington, Boyle, Casey, Taylor, LaRue and Nelson counties.

Besides Lebanon, the incorporated cities are Loretto and Bradfordsville. Smaller communities include Gravel Switch, Nerinx, Raywick and St. Mary. Wikipedia notes that planar maps place the geographic center of Kentucky about three miles north-northwest of Lebanon, just off KY 429, though neighboring counties dispute the exact spot.

One school system covers the whole county: the Marion County School District, whose comprehensive high school is Marion County High School. Lebanon also has the Marion County Public Library. A seller with a rural parcel should know that farmland is assessed at agricultural use value under Section 172A of the Kentucky Constitution, while the barns and fencing on it are valued by replacement cost less depreciation. That split can matter when a farm with a house on it goes up for sale.

Growth has been flat. Population was 19,820 in 2010 and 19,581 in 2020, and the July 2025 estimate is 20,115.

sections.h2: How do Marion County housing numbers compare?
sections.html:
Marion County is mostly owner-occupied and mid-priced for Kentucky. The 2020 to 2024 Census figures put roughly three of every four households in homes they own.

The 91.9 percent figure for staying in the same house is high, and only 56 building permits were issued in 2025, so new construction is thin. Persons aged 65 and over make up 19.5 percent of the county, which is relevant to the homestead exemption covered below.

sections.h2: What are the Marion County property tax payment dates?
sections.html:
The sheriff mails bills before October 1 and runs the collection calendar below, according to the office's FAQ. If no bill arrives by October 10, call and the office will mail one.

  • October 1 to November 1: 2% discount
  • November 2 to December 31: face amount
  • January 1 to January 31: 5% penalty
  • February 1 to April 15: 21% penalty
  • April 16: unpaid bills are transferred to the County Clerk for collection

The 21 percent figure combines the 10 percent penalty in KRS 134.015 with the sheriff's add-on from KRS 134.119. The sheriff's system does not track partial payments, so plan to pay the whole bill in one transaction. By mail, put the bill number on the check and enclose a stamped, self-addressed envelope if you want a receipt. Credit cards are taken in person only, and the card company's fee falls on the payer.

Mortgage escrow does not change who receives the paper bill. The sheriff mails bills to homeowners, and it is up to the homeowner to pass the bill to the lender in time.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax when a Marion County house changes hands?
sections.html:
The person who owned the property on January 1 is named on the bill, even if the house sells later in the year. The sheriff says the bill should then be forwarded in care of the buyer. A buyer who never gets a bill can ask the sheriff's office to mail one.

The sheriff states plainly that the office is not responsible when a bill is missed because of oversights during the closing. Put the proration and the payoff on the settlement statement, and have the closing agent confirm payment with the sheriff before funds go out.

Under KRS 134.015(4), unpaid tax is a personal debt of the taxpayer on the assessment date, and a lien continues for up to eleven years under KRS 134.420 no matter who owns the property afterward. Delinquent bills sit with the clerk, who also runs a free Online Deed Room. Call 270-692-2651 for a payoff.

sections.h2: How can a Marion County owner challenge a valuation?
sections.html:
Contact the PVA at 270-692-3401 and ask for a conference. That is the required first step, and KRS 133.120 says the PVA or a deputy must explain how your value was reached and keep a record of the meeting.

If the conference does not settle it, a written petition goes to the County Clerk by one workday after the inspection period ends. It should identify the parcel, give your reasons and state what you believe the property is worth. The county board of assessment appeals then hears the case. Under KRS 133.030 it convenes 25 to 35 days after inspection closes.

  • Bring evidence such as a recent appraisal, comparable sales, an insurance policy or a repair estimate.
  • You may record the hearing, and the board must visit the property if you ask.
  • Keep paying on the value you claim. An appeal does not pause collection.

The Department of Revenue says the PVA must physically inspect every parcel at least once in four years, so a visit by PVA staff to your street is routine.

sections.h2: How much is the Marion County homestead exemption?
sections.html:
It is $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years, set by the Department of Revenue. You qualify as a homeowner who is 65 or older, or who is classified as totally disabled, and the home must be your permanent residence.

Take the Census median home value of $168,100 as an example. After the exemption the taxable assessment would be $119,000. Once an age-based application is accepted, it carries forward for as long as the same owner lives in the house. For married couples, only one exemption applies per household. The exemption does not move with the property, so a buyer must apply separately. The sheriff directs homestead and disability questions to the PVA.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Marion County?
sections.html:
Kentucky's transfer tax under KRS 142.050 is $0.50 per $500 of value or part of $500, and the Marion County Clerk collects it before taking the deed. On a $168,100 sale the tax works out to $168.50.

The clerk's website lists weekday hours plus Saturday mornings, which helps a seller who works through the week, and says taxes paid there can be paid by cash, check, debit or credit card with extra fees for cards. Ask the clerk for the current recording charge. Note that foreclosures, parent-to-child gifts and transfers between divorcing spouses are exempt from the transfer tax.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Marion County property taxes?
faqs.a: Pay the Marion County Sheriff's Office at 223 North Spalding Avenue, Suite 101 in Lebanon, or call 270-692-3051. Checks by mail need the bill number written on them.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for paying Marion County taxes in February?
faqs.a: The sheriff lists a 21 percent penalty from February 1 through April 15. January costs 5 percent, and on April 16 the bill moves to the County Clerk.

faqs.q: Can I make a partial payment on my Marion County tax bill?
faqs.a: Not reliably. The sheriff's FAQ says the office's system does not track partial payments, so pay the full amount during the discount or face-amount window.

faqs.q: Who do I call about the Marion County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Call the Property Valuation Administrator at 270-692-3401. The sheriff's office refers all exemption and valuation questions there.

faqs.q: How do I find out if a Marion County property has delinquent taxes?
faqs.a: Ask the County Clerk at 270-692-2651. The sheriff's FAQ says delinquent bills are transferred to the clerk, and the clerk's Online Deed Room is free to use.
